findings.topic: Hypertrophy rep ranges / volume, advanced trainee
findings.summary: Advanced trainees generally need higher total weekly volume per muscle group than beginners/intermediates to continue progressing, typically working in the 6-15 rep range across multiple exercises, often needing more exercise variety or technique variation (tempo, unilateral work, paused reps) since simple linear load progression stalls faster at this stage.
findings.source: Schoenfeld, B. — Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy, 2nd ed. (chapter summary)

findings.summary: Kettlebells, bands, and bodyweight/pull-up-bar work can support continued muscle gain for an advanced trainee if volume, time-under-tension, and exercise variation are managed deliberately (e.g. slower tempos, unilateral and single-limb variations, shorter rest for metabolic stress) to compensate for the lack of easy heavy-load progression.
findings.source: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed. (resistance training modalities chapter summary)

findings.summary: A push/pull/legs plus upper/lower rotation (5 sessions) is a common, well-tolerated structure for advanced trainees wanting higher weekly frequency per movement pattern without the single-muscle-group isolation of classic bodybuilding splits.
findings.source: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed. (program design chapter summary)
